rule: An entry is published only with a link to the vendor's own page. Wording stays neutral and describes only what the source says.

integrations.statement: KAPE keeps the EZ Tools binaries in its Modules folder and runs them as modules to parse what it collects. KAPE itself is free for many uses but is not open source.

Documented in AXIOM 2.0 (2018): the product integrates core plugins from the Volatility framework, so examiners can run memory analysis inside AXIOM and see processes, drivers, DLLs and network connections.
Documented in 2022: AXIOM Cyber processes YARA rules, ships with a set of common rules, lets users add their own, and can pull rules from a Git repository link. Matches appear as artifacts.
Documented in 2024: the ATT&CK integration in AXIOM Cyber can run Sigma rules to identify techniques, and the post suggests using them on Windows event logs and Linux audit logs.
Documented in 2020: custom artifacts written by the iLEAPP author let AXIOM process iLEAPP parser output. They were shared through the Magnet Artifact Exchange.
Documented in 2020: a Magnet employee wrote Artifact Exchange custom artifacts for bulk_extractor output, so that results from the open tool can be loaded into AXIOM.
Magnet Forensics publishes this open repository, a .NET wrapper for libyara that gives C# and PowerShell code a simpler way to use the YARA scanning engine.
This Magnet Forensics repository holds a native video library. Its README says it needs an LGPL static build of ffmpeg 5.1.x, which is not included, and suggests vcpkg for compiling FFmpeg.
Belkasoft X can apply YARA rules during data source analysis and lists matched files with offsets and conditions. The page says this is available in the Corporate edition only.
Belkasoft X can apply Sigma rules to Windows event logs and shows the matched rule name, product and category. The page says this is available in the Corporate edition only.
Belkasoft says the product integrates Volatility features for memory analysis. Users download Volatility separately and point Belkasoft X to its executable in the settings.
Belkasoft X can use hashcat to brute-force some password hashes found during analysis. The help page covers attack modes such as mask and dictionary, plus extra hashcat arguments.
Vendor update post: open-source YARA rules from ReversingLabs are already included for computer collections. Users can also import or write their own rules and pick rule sets before a scan.

An EnCase App Central script (release 1.5.0, 2024) makes Volatility easier to use in EnCase, with multithreading. It needs the standalone Volatility program and is listed as not tested with Volatility 3.
An EnCase App Central script scans selected items with YARA rule files through the libyara.NET API. Release 2.1 (August 2024) targets YARA 4.5.1. Results go to bookmarks and optional JSON.

A script in the Nuix GitHub organisation links YARA to Nuix Workbench. Selected case items are scanned with chosen rules and matches become tags. It is under Apache 2.0 and was last tested in Nuix 9.0.
Nuix blog guide: the RegRipper extension for Nuix Workstation works with RegRipper downloaded from its GitHub page and extracted on the analysis system. A matching extension exists for YARA.

integrations.open_source: hashcat and John the Ripper rule syntax
integrations.statement: Passware says its Apply Rules attack is compatible with the rule syntax of hashcat and John the Ripper, and it checks rule files made for those tools.
Release post for 2026 v1: Passware Kit can recover ZIP passwords from hash files extracted with the Zip2John tool, which belongs to John the Ripper.
Amped blog (2024): FIVE offers separate video engines, including an FFMS engine described as built on FFmpeg and an FFmpeg engine that uses the native FFmpeg decoder.
Elcomsoft blog (May 2023): the toolkit has almost eighty sub-projects, many of them open source. The company says it must publish its changes to those under their permissive licences.
The page says AIR can run YARA, Sigma and osquery rulesets across many endpoints. Users can write their own rules or deploy rules from a shared library.

integrations.open_source: YARA, Sigma, osquery and Suricata rule formats
integrations.statement: The knowledge base names YARA, Sigma, osquery and Suricata as the rule formats its detection engineering feature can generate, validate, convert and test.

integrations.product: Cisco XDR Forensics (MITRE ATT&CK Analyzer, DRONE)
integrations.open_source: Sigma rules from SigmaHQ and Hayabusa
integrations.statement: The changelog says many releases update DRONE with the latest Sigma rules taken from the SigmaHQ and Hayabusa repositories. Releases are listed from 2024 to 2026.
For higher license tiers, the Rapid7 Agent carries a client-only build of Velociraptor, so users can pivot to it during investigations. Some open-source features are turned off.
Rapid7 says Velociraptor is its open-source DFIR framework, added to InsightIDR. Community artifacts are written in VQL, and alerts link to the matching Velociraptor endpoint page.
A Rapid7 post says data gathered with a Velociraptor offline collector can be imported into the Cado platform, which processes it and builds timelines. Documented in 2024.
Sumo Logic documents a pySigma plugin that turns Sigma rules into Cloud SIEM rule JSON, which can be imported by API or UI. Field mappings cover 70 or more log sources.
A Microsoft blog, updated in 2022, shows a notebook that uses the sigmac converter to turn Sigma rules into KQL for Sentinel. Only a subset of rules converts.
Livehunt applies YARA rules to files that VirusTotal analyzes. The page says it uses an up-to-date YARA version and lists the YARA modules it allows.
Users can run custom YARA rules on Windows, Linux and macOS endpoints. Rules can be chosen from Response Management or uploaded as a YARA or text file under 1 MB.
The YARA Scan task scans objects against rules in .yara or .yar files that follow YARA 4.0.2. A matching rule produces a verdict that is written to the log.
A Sophos community post (2021) says XDR live queries expose osquery tables and let users write SQL against them. It lists the osquery versions used on Windows, Mac and Linux.
The same 2021 post says the osquery YARA table in Sophos XDR takes a signature file and a path and searches for matching files.
Bitdefender describes YARA rules as queries that scan endpoints for malicious patterns and raise alerts or incidents. Up to 50 rules are allowed and the include directive is not supported.
Tanium's own Tech Talk says Threat Response supports detection formats including OpenIOC, STIX, Tanium Signals and YARA rules.
Cisco's guide says advanced custom detection signatures are built into a database, and tells users to check the ClamAV folder on the endpoint to confirm the new signature set arrived.
The default parser list includes parsers for osquery logs, Zeek (Bro) logs and ClamAV logs, so these sources can be ingested into the SIEM.
Kroll's Q3 2022 KAPE update says the modules for Hayabusa were updated, renamed and moved into their own folder.
The same Q3 2022 update says the Chainsaw module was changed to match the syntax of Chainsaw 2.0 and newer.
A Splunk-hosted GitHub add-on parses osquery logs and results into Splunk fields and data models. It is documented and tested on macOS only.
Splunk's Lantern article says Sigma rules must be translated for Splunk. It says the Recorded Future app handles the translation and mapping, and users can then edit the search.
Elastic's public repository for its endpoint detection logic has a folder of YARA rules for malware protection. The repository is under the Elastic License 2.0.
Elastic documents an integration that polls the REST API of a MISP instance and indexes its events and attributes as threat data, with decay scores for expiring indicators.
Corelight describes Zeek as the core analysis engine of its sensors. Corelight adds management, fleet and log export features on top.
Corelight v19 runs Zeek and Suricata on the same sensor. Suricata alert logs carry the Zeek UID so analysts can jump to the related Zeek logs.

integrations.product: Clear NDR Enterprise (formerly Stamus Security Platform)
integrations.statement: Stamus says the product uses Suricata as its foundation and adds asset visibility, alert triage and other detection features. Stamus handles Suricata updates for customers.
Cisco's adoption guide says Snort 3 is the inspection engine path for Secure Firewall, with Snort 2 still supported. Custom Snort 2 rules are not syntax-compatible with Snort 3.
Strata Cloud Manager can convert Snort and Suricata rules into custom threat signatures for its firewalls. Rules can be uploaded as a text file or pasted in.
Sysdig presents Sysdig Secure as an extension of Falco, the runtime detection project it created in 2016 and donated to the CNCF in 2017.
The Elastic integration reads Suricata's eve.json log file through Elastic Agent and sends the events to Elastic for alerting and threat hunting.
The Elastic integration reads Zeek JSON logs such as conn, dns, http, ssl and files through Elastic Agent and maps them to the Elastic Common Schema.
The integration manages osquery on Elastic Agents through Fleet. Users run live or scheduled SQL queries from Kibana and results are stored in Elasticsearch.
The AWS partner list names Prowler, an open source AWS security checking tool, as a third-party product that sends findings to Security Hub.
Nozomi's threat intelligence documentation says its YARA rules follow the YARA specification and are applied to files seen in HTTP and SMB transfers.
The open source licence file for Sophos Firewall 20.0 lists snort (partly) under GPL v2.
The product manual states that X-Ways Forensics contains an unofficial build of libPFF, which is governed by the LGPL.
The CleverFiles licence exhibit lists The Sleuth Kit, distributed under the IBM Public License and the Common Public License.
The CleverFiles licence exhibit names libimobiledevice, with libplist and libusbmuxd, for Disk Drill for Mac.
The acknowledgments page says the program includes the ExifTool utility by Phil Harvey, used under the Perl Artistic License. Documented around the 2013 copyright years.
Binalyze's open source software list names YARA version 4.5.1, the go-yara binding and YARA rule sets from ReversingLabs.

open_on_open.open_source: The Sleuth Kit, Plaso and iLEAPP
open_on_open.statement: Autopsy describes itself as a graphical platform for The Sleuth Kit and other tools. Its standard ingest modules include a Plaso module for timelines and an iOS analyser based on iLEAPP.
